newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Longer OLOs seen higher on shift out of short end.
newsitem.headline: Longer OLOs seen higher on shift out of short end.

text.p: The longer end of the Belgian bond yield curve should benefit in the next few months from a recovery after recent sales as players re-train their sights on low inflation and interest rates, dealers said on Tuesday.

They expected an end to a flurry of activity at the short end in the wake of the U.S. Fed's recent rate rise decision, which pushed yields up. "That correction went too far," Kredietbank analyst Conrad Fieremans said.
Recently, cash had flowed into the short end, but the upward scope there had dried up now. The pendulum should swing to the longer end, especially after today's OLO exchange auction.
"Today we will find out whether players are keen to lengthen duration," a trader said.

At the OLO exchange auction the Treasury is offering OLO 25 (5.00 pct, March 2001), 10 (8.75 pct, June 2002), 19 (6.50 pct, March 2005) and 26 (6.25 pct, March 2007) against OLO 15 (6.75 pct, May 1997) and OLO 8 (9.25 pct, August 1997).

Dealers expected attention to centre on the new 10-year benchmark, OLO 26. The paper was quoted at 101.47 to yield 6.05 percent at 1025 GMT, down from an opening 101.70, with the price seeing the usual pre-auction pressure.
Fieremans expected the yield to ease to 5.80 or 5.85 percent in the next one or two months. Other analysts have targetted levels around 5.90 percent by the end of the second quarter.

Dealers expected the market to remain relatively quiet until Friday when U.S. inflation data are due. U.S. March PPIs are forecast to come out slightly firmer month-on-month, but easier year-on-year on the back of the dollar's strength, which will have capped imported inflation. Retail sales numbers are expected to show growth slowed in March compared with February, which should give bonds further support.
